title: Inca conquest of the Chimú kingdom
summary: Around 1470 the Inca, led by Tupac Yupanqui, captured the Chimú ruler Minchançaman and made the Chimú kingdom a vassal state within the Inca empire. The king was held at Cuzco, and the Inca moved thousands of Chimú artisans, with their finest pieces, from the capital Chan Chan to Cuzco.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia gives c. 1470; Encyclopedia.com says between 1460 and 1470 and, elsewhere, by 1470.

as_recorded.value: captured the 11th known Chimú ruler Minchançaman c. 1470 CE
The Incas had conquered the Chimú between 1460 and 1470

where.modern_name: Chan Chan, Huanchaco, Trujillo, La Libertad, Peru (pin at the Chimú capital, not a battle site)
where.historical_name: Chan Chan, capital of the Chimú kingdom (Chimor), conquered by the Inca

importance.justification: Ended the largest coastal kingdom of the Andes and added its capital, labour and metalwork to the Inca empire.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Chan Chan, Peru

reviewer_note: Least sure of the year: sources give c. 1470 or a range from 1460. The pin is the capital (Encyclopedia.com calls Chan Chan the imperial capital), not a battlefield. Encyclopedia.com does not name the Inca commander; Tupac Yupanqui comes from World History Encyclopedia.
